thread:
maya: Pushed a quick eval comparing 3 template variants across US/EU/APAC queries — saw an odd reversal in NDCG order for APAC. attaching top-level numbers.
sam: can you paste the exact command/seed? sample size? :thinking:
maya: ran with seed=42, n=10k queries per region, model=rerank-v3-ptq (int8), baseline=f16. command:
```
./eval_runner --model rerank-v3-ptq --templates templA,templB,templC --regions US,EU,APAC --seed 42 --n_queries 10000
```
alex: numbers? summary pls.
maya: summary (NDCG@10 / MRR):
- US: templA 0.724 / 0.481, templB 0.719 / 0.474, templC 0.711 / 0.468
- EU: templA 0.701 / 0.459, templB 0.703 / 0.462, templC 0.698 / 0.456
- APAC: templA 0.689 / 0.447, templB 0.696 / 0.453, templC 0.705 / 0.462  <-- templC beats others here
sam: weird. templC is the most verbose prompt, right? Could be interacting with tokenization/priming.
ajax: (typo) alex: yeah templC adds country-specific phrasing + polite prefix. maybe localization helps APAC queries.
alex: is this held out eval set stratified by locale or just region tag? if stratified, distribution of query lengths might differ.
maya: region tag only; no stratification beyond that. APAC queries skew longer, more formal language in our sample.
jin: could be amplification of a calibration bias after int8 quant. do we have f16 numbers for templC by region?
maya: f16 templC: US 0.726/0.483, EU 0.705/0.464, APAC 0.707/0.463 — APAC gap smaller but still templC > templA in f16 too.
sam: so not pure quant artifact. maybe templC aligns better with APAC query style.
alex: do we see differences in candidate scoring spread? stddev of scores or margin between top-1/top-2?
maya: quick stats for APAC templA vs templC (int8): avg top1-score: templA 0.62, templC 0.66; top2: templA 0.58, templC 0.60; margin +0.04 vs +0.06.
jin: looks like templC increases separation. maybe priming reduces ambiguous ties.
eval-bot: Automated fairness check ran: templC APAC vs US NDCG delta = -0.018 (APAC lower than US) but templC reduces that gap by 0.005 vs templA. p-value (paired bootstrap) templC vs templA on APAC: 0.032.
sam: p=0.032 suggests real effect but small. Any churn on top queries (manual inspect)?
maya: sampled 50 APAC queries where templC changed top-1. ~32/50 actually looked qualitatively better, 12 neutral, 6 worse.
alex: sounds promising. next steps: (1) rerun with stratified holdout controlling for query length & formality, (2) run with different seeds and n=30k to improve significance, (3) try templC with a shorter variant to see if verbosity is main driver.
jin: also test templC with a tighter truncation policy; longer priming might push candidate context out for long queries.
maya: will kick off runs tonight, enabling debug logs for 100 changed queries. logging command:
```
./eval_runner --model rerank-v3-ptq --templates templC_short,templC_full --regions APAC --seed 7 --n_queries 30000 --log_changes 100
```
sam: assign a follow-up PR to add templ identifiers in eval metadata (so downstream we can filter by priming).
alex: good. if templC sustains lift and no regressions elsewhere, consider adding as a recommended template in onboard docs.
maya: noted. will post results in this thread tomorrow. :coffee:
